reasons: The candidate multiplies by the constant 100, which is not in the Datadog source. This violates the no-invented-constants rule and changes the quantity and unit.

The PromQL averages raw rate series per image, but the metric has device_major/device_minor series per container. The average therefore runs over devices as well as containers, while Datadog averages one value per container. A per-container sum (by container_name, container_image_name) before the average would match the Datadog grain.

The unit of docker.io.read_bytes is not established. If it is bytes/s, the rate() of a bytes sum is comparable; any scaling must be justified in notes with a documentation link, not applied in promql.
The metric is a monotonic sum with unit By, so rate() on it is allowed, and the operation="read" matcher and the dropped unprefixed $scope template variable are correct.
